conviction_note: The print turns on one disclosure: what Bank OZK says about the $915M IQHQ/RaDD San Diego construction loan, which it rated pass at Q2, which passed maturity in August and which got a 6-week forbearance-style extension to Oct 9 that Citi flagged (stock -5%). The core quarter sets up a little better than consensus: the EPS bar of $1.43-1.45 sits below Q2's $1.49, the Fed hiked on Sep 16 and OZK is asset-sensitive, and peer credit looks benign. Short interest is also crowded at about 16-17% of float with 12.5-13.5 days to cover, so a benign IQHQ outcome could squeeze. The findings sum to +0.9 because the small positives outnumber the one negative. The scaled number is 0 (p_up 50, abs 5.5) because the IQHQ disclosure is a binary of unknown sign that can swamp all of them.

findings.finding: Bank OZK's $915M construction loan to IQHQ on the vacant 1.7M SF RaDD life-science campus in San Diego was rated PASS at Q2 (Gleason on the July 21 call: 'if our thoughts in that regard change, we'll make appropriate adjustments'). It then passed its August maturity and got only a ~6-week extension to Oct 9, signed Sep 30 / Oct 1 but effective Aug 26, which Citi called a 'brief forbearance period' (shares -5% the week of Oct 7). The Q3 release is the first document that must show how the loan was graded at 9/30. A downgrade to substandard or nonaccrual would roughly triple nonperforming loans (Q2 NPLs ~$300M) and could bring a specific reserve against a $461.5M allowance. The alternative management promised is a multi-year extension plus recap with the mezz lender, which would be read as a relief. Management said it will update on the Oct 21 call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline has no print history because OZK files with the FDIC, not EDGAR. On this exact loan, the Citi note alone took the stock down more than 5% in the week of 2026-10-07 (Bisnow, CRE Daily). Q2 2026 charge-offs of $56.2M (vs $8.2M a year earlier) came with an EPS beat, and the stock is down ~9% since that print.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the -5% Citi drop is the market pricing the risk that the loan is impaired. What it cannot price is the 9/30 risk grade, the reserve and the terms of any recap, none of which are public; nothing after the Oct 9 maturity has been reported. If a nonaccrual-plus-reserve outcome were fully priced, the skew would be put-bid; it is flat (+0.48), and the stock has rallied off its one-month low since Oct 13.
findings.independence: Sponsor distress comes from a different source: Bisnow 2026-03-19 (https://www.bisnow.com/news/national/life-sciences/iqhq-facing-downgrades-confronts-challenges-leasing-market-133748). Six funds marked IQHQ down in 2H25; IQHQ is not paying interest on its Bluerock PIK loans; RaDD is over half of IQHQ's operating portfolio; San Diego lab vacancy is 28.6% and JLL sees no large tenant for RaDD; its only announced lab tenant is JCVI (~50k SF). CRE Daily 2026-10-08 (https://www.credaily.com/briefs/bank-ozk-falls-5-after-citi-flags-915m-san-diego-loan/) rests on the same Bisnow/Citi report and is not independent. The Q2 call transcript (MarketBeat) is the primary source for the pass rating.

findings.finding: IQHQ kept access to outside capital at the start of Q4. On 2026-10-01, Innovative Industrial Properties (IIPR) committed a $245M mezzanine loan to IQHQ affiliates for Alewife Park Phase I in Cambridge at ~15.8% (14% floor), repaying an $85M bridge, with an option to buy up to $155M more of the other mezz lender's notes. That raises the odds that a mezz-led recap of RaDD, which OZK said it was negotiating, can be funded. It is a different project and costly capital, so it is weak evidence.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior OZK print to compare against; this item bears on how the IQHQ disclosure is received.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits in an IIPR 8-K that does not name RaDD or OZK. Neither Bisnow nor CRE Daily, in their Oct 7-8 OZK coverage, connected it to the RaDD recap, so bank analysts would not see it unless they followed IQHQ's capital stack.
findings.independence: Bisnow 2026-03-19 reports IQHQ raised $900M of rescue financing in Jan 2025 and a $270M IIPR package in Aug 2025, so the sponsor has repeatedly found capital, at punitive terms. The same article also documents the distress, so it points both ways.

findings.finding: The Fed raised the funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 (first hike since 2023), and minutes show most policymakers projecting another hike by year-end. OZK's loan book is largely floating-rate RESG construction loans, so a hike reprices assets ahead of its CD-heavy deposits. The Q2-call NIM guide ('a little under' Q1's 4.20%) was set before the hike, which gives room for a firmer Q4 NII/NIM outlook. Higher rates should also slow the ~$2.5-3B/quarter of RESG payoffs that have shrunk loans year on year. This is macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Unknown from the baseline. A 2024 CRE Daily item records OZK guiding NIM down on an expected cutting cycle, so management does talk the rate path into its NIM guide.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (page on the September 2026 FOMC and minutes)
findings.why_not_priced: Only two weeks of the hike fall in Q3, so the effect shows in the Q4 guide, not the quarter. The EPS consensus is still below Q2's actual ($1.43-1.45 vs $1.49), which does not look like analysts have marked NII up for a hike. Some of it is surely in the analysts' models.
findings.independence: Western Alliance's Q3 release (2026-10-19, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001212545/000162828026066286/pressrelease-9302026.htm) shows NIM up 4bp QoQ on higher asset yields. Zions' Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000109380/000010938026000125/exh991earningsrelease20260.htm) shows NIM down year on year, so the peer read is mixed.

findings.finding: Excluding IQHQ, the core quarter faces a low bar. Consensus EPS of $1.43-1.45 is below Q2's $1.49, and revenue consensus of $433.3M is barely above Q2's $430.0M. On the Q2 call management guided average earning assets up in Q3 and Q4, payoffs 'more levelized', provisions to 'drift down', and said ~$175M of the prior $200M buyback had been used below tangible book, with a new $200M authorization in place. That buyback matters at a stock price of ~0.89x book.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat EPS by $0.01 and missed revenue, and the stock is down ~9% since. Q1 2026 was reported as a narrow EPS miss (unverified aggregator). Small EPS beats have not been rewarded.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits below the last actual even though management guided earning assets up, so analysts appear to have haircut for credit cost or payoffs. If they had priced the guide, Q3 EPS would sit at or above $1.49. That gap is the room for a core beat, unless IQHQ eats it through the provision line.
findings.independence: Consensus figures come from Benzinga and Earnings Whispers (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/x/OZK). Q2 actuals are from Talk Business 2026-07-21. Both share the same transcript-based guidance.

findings.finding: Peer read-through on credit is benign. Western Alliance's Q3 2026 release (Oct 19) shows nonaccruals down $77M to 0.79% of loans, classified assets down $37M, flat provision, construction and land loans flat, and NIM up. That is a sector backdrop in which one large OZK credit is less likely to be read as systemic.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measurable from the baseline. OZK's moves in Sep-Oct 2026 tracked regional-bank sector days (per an aggregator).
findings.why_not_priced: It reported one day before OZK and is mostly priced into the sector already. It is filed small because it is a peer proxy, not OZK's own number.
findings.independence: The Zions Q3 release (2026-10-19) shows NII up 2% but NIM down year on year. It is neutral rather than confirming.

findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the market's own bet against the print, so this is not unpriced information. It matters as an asymmetry in how the IQHQ outcome moves the stock.

findings.finding: The board raised the common dividend to $0.49 (+2.1%, the 65th consecutive quarterly increase) on 2026-10-01, the day after OZK signed the IQHQ amendment (Sep 30). That is a small signal that the board did not see a capital-threatening loss in hand.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is a routine quarterly increase, so it is likely ignored.
findings.why_not_priced: Already public and routine. The only new reading is the timing relative to the IQHQ amendment, which nobody in the coverage pointed out.
findings.independence: Bisnow 2026-10-07 gives the Sep 30 / Oct 1 amendment signing dates.

baseline_tension: Neither the flat skew (+0.48) nor the -2% 20-day run-up states a direction. The heavy put/call OI and the 16-17% short interest are the market's bearish lean, and they match the IQHQ negative, which is why that finding is sized well below its downside tail. The core-quarter and rate positives run against the positioning.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short shrinks a negative): IQHQ finding -1.5 -> -1.3 given 16.9% SI / 13.5 DTC; kept largely intact because rule 2 says an unquantified reported-quarter impairment is the exception that has paid.
Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission unconfirmed by the company): Fed-hike NIM finding +0.8 -> +0.5.
Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; small EPS beats were not rewarded in Q2): core-bar finding +0.7 -> +0.5.
Positioning finding +0.5 -> +0.4 (positioning is the market's bet, not unpriced information).
